Western Australia’s Stanley College opens new hospitality training hub  

By Maia Hart 31/07/2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:45
Instaread

Stanley College’s West Perth campus has officially opened, which includes a new hospitality training hub designed to equip students with the practical skills and real-world learning opportunities.  

The Hay Street site is the third local campus for the college, and was officially opened by The Hon. Roger Cook MLA, Premier of Western Australia.  

The purpose built campus has been designed to bridge the gap between education and employment, and provide students with hands-on experience in commercial-standard hospitality environments reflecting workplaces they will enter after graduation.  

This includes CU29 Restaurant, a commercial training restaurant that provides students the opportunity to serve real customers and therefore developing the technical capability, professionalism, and confidence needed in the industry.  

The site supports commercial cookery students undertaking qualifications from Certificate III through to Advanced Diploma, and includes pathways into degree-level study. It will also benefit students studying a Bachelor of Business Majoring in Hospitality and a Master of Business in Hospitality.  

Stanley College Board of Directors Chair Alberto Tassone says the purpose-built campus represents a new approach to hospitality education. 

“Our students will learn in commercial-standard kitchens, modern training restaurants and  contemporary hospitality environments that mirror the workplaces they will enter after graduation,” says Tassone.  

“Learning here is not simply theoretical, it is hands-on. Students gain real-world experience serving actual customers while completing their practical training and assessment. 

“This is an investment not only in our students but in Western Australia’s hospitality industry and the skilled workforce it needs for the future.” 

The opening also marks a new chapter following the recent appointment of Chief Executive Officer Chien Vu.
